This needs more details I think to state how static EID is injected in an EM config.

Do we intend to merge the platform init code that injects static EID (or merged already? if not, please add link here)

This assumes only one EID per config? Alon8 has multiple, right?

Is this for the bridge or endpoints behind the bridge?
this is making it endpoint agnostic. We shouldn't assume what the bridging structure is in this daemon. An instance of the resulting classes will just get made for what we find behind a given eid.
This wouldn't work on platforms where EM configs for some devices include `StaticEid` and EM configs for other devices do not include it, correct?
Can you unpack this statement a bit? What does it mean?

yeah, this is a bit terse.

We don't have MCTPoUSB support in MctpReactor today (needed generally for interacting with this at least on a large number of platforms), nor do we have support for determining device identity of bridged endpoints. i.e. if I have, say, a bridge with 8 endpoints behind it, there's no way to today to map out eid X is device Y and route through inventory when they're behind a bridge. This is made more complicated yet because the existing EntityManager schemes also lack a way to talk about hubs and USB topologies, so tracing device identity through multiple instantiations of a given entity manager config is not feasible today.

This at least gives us some (crude) way to support multiple GPU's and have a way to talk about which endpoint is which. Previously, multiple GPU's and SMA's would cause an exception because of the existing code in NvidiaGpuDeviceDiscovery.cpp starting effectively at the top of the query to MCTPd to find endpoints. That is patchable (i.e. skip eids that already exist), but without a concrete way to talk about device identity it makes the inventory non deterministic, i.e. GPU sensor names may not match between BMC reboots, dependent on device probe order and kernel implementation details such as network interface name assignment.

That said, I also have a patch set coming up that I prefer to this, mostly because this is a bit of hackery without the aforementioned MCTPReactor support, where we get callbacks through dbus when a new device is registered with mctpd, and we'll send device queries to devices that support PCI IANA commands, similar to how PLDMd works today. Once that goes up, I'll likely abandon this patch. This was mostly needed to do initial nvl32-obmc bringup and do bug crushing in this daemon (see other recent patches in this area).



Let me know if any more clarification is required, thanks.

> This is made more complicated yet because the existing EntityManager schemes also lack a way to talk about hubs and USB topologies, so tracing device identity through multiple instantiations of a given entity manager config is not feasible today.

I expect the right thing to do is progress this:

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77381

Let's fix it properly?

Though it sounds like fixing it properly might be on the radar?

Consider marking this as WIP if there's no plan to get it merged.
yeah, I'll mark it as a WIP. Fixing it properly is on the radar.
